chunks.arabic_text: مَعَانِي الْأَخْبَارِ: ابْنُ الْوَلِيدِ، عَنِ الصَّفَّارِ، عَنۡ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَىٰ، عَنِ الْأَهْوَازِيِّ، عَنِ ابْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ، عَنۡ حَمَّادٍ، عَنِ الْحَلَبِيِّ قَالَ

translations.en: Ma'ani al-Akhbar: Ibn al-Walid, from al-Saffar, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Ahwazi, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi who said:

chunks.arabic_text: قُلۡتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ: مَا أَدْنَىٰ مَا يَكُونُ بِهِ الْعَبْدُ كَافِرًا؟ قَالَ: أَنْ يَبْتَدِعَ شَيْئًا فَيَتَوَلَّىٰ عَلَيْهِ وَيَبْرَأَ مِمَّنْ خَالَفَهُ

translations.en: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): What is the least thing by which the slave becomes Kafir? He said: That he innovates something, then associates solely with it and disassociates from the one who opposes him.

en.summary: This hadith defines the minimum threshold for a person to be considered a disbeliever (Kafir) through the act of religious innovation (Bid'ah). It specifies that innovating a new belief or practice, then fully committing to it while disassociating from those who differ from it, constitutes Kufr.
en.seo_question: What is the minimum condition for a Muslim to become a disbeliever according to Imam al-Sadiq?

key_terms.مِمَّنْ خَالَفَهُ: from the one who opposes him
